items.abstract: <jats:p>Highway infrastructure full lifecycle management, ranging from planning and design to operation and maintenance, involves complex multi-stage, multi-agent, and multi-source data coordination problems. This paper proposes a collaborative decision-making framework based on a heterogeneous multi-agent system, encapsulating planner, design, construction, maintenance, and budget agents as autonomous units with independent perception, reasoning, and decision-making capabilities. Blockchain technology is employed to ensure trustworthy data sharing among agents, while a MAPPO-based deep reinforcement learning algorithm optimizes cross-stage collaboration strategies under a 30-year planning horizon. To support training and evaluation, we construct a Highway Lifecycle Management Simulator (HLMS) integrating SUMO traffic simulation, AASHTO pavement and bridge degradation models, and Life Cycle Cost Analysis (LCCA). A case study of a highway expansion project in Jiangsu Province validates the framework&apos;s effectiveness in scheme comparison efficiency and maintenance fund allocation optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with traditional LCCA methods and representative reinforcement learning baselines, the proposed framework achieves over 15\% reduction in the Net Present Value (NPV) of total lifecycle costs and over 20\% reduction in annual Vehicle Hours of Delay (VHD). The results show that multi-agent cross-stage collaboration can significantly improve the intelligence level and decision quality of highway full lifecycle management.</jats:p>
title: A Multi-Agent Collaborative Decision-Making Framework for Highway Full Lifecycle Management
